title: Scheduler-driven structured task checkpoint and task-switch effect canary

definitions.structuredCheckpoint: A source-citing, closed task-state record containing objective, completed work, constraints, and one normalized next action.
definitions.taskSwitch: Three distinct Scheduler Runs in one Module process: checkpoint task A, complete unrelated task B without task A active context, then resume task A from stored evidence.
definitions.sameProcess: All three Runs use one process-isolated Extension host and one Module generation; this does not claim Linux control-group ownership.
definitions.baseline: The same Scheduler, child implementation, model descriptor, and three task messages without tool-invocation or storage access.

question: Can one Scheduler-driven process-isolated Agent store a sourced task checkpoint, finish an unrelated task with no task-A state in its active model context, and later resume the exact next action from that checkpoint, while the paired no-tool baseline cannot resume?

primary.statement: The structured-checkpoint condition completes checkpoint_store, answers the unrelated task, then completes checkpoint_list and checkpoint_get before committing the exact sourced next action; the paired no-tool baseline reports that it cannot resume.

guardrails.statement: Neither task-B model input nor the first resume planning input contains task-A objective value, completed-step values, constraint values, checkpoint key, source ID, or next-action values before retrieval; generic checkpoint schema field names are not treated as state values.
Each condition uses three distinct Runs in one Module generation, commits all three Scheduler jobs, closes every capability effect, and stops only its recorded child.
The treatment child receives model-operation and tool-invocation only; it never receives raw storage, provider endpoint, credential, authorization, or another capability handle in model-visible data.

decision.currentProductState: Scheduler, process Host, active-Run model and tool capabilities, persistent tool/effect journals, and file Core are product components, but product bootstrap still refuses every configured Module. Versions 1 through 4 exposed and closed baseline, storage-abstraction, and validator defects. Version 5 made no Agent change and stopped on its first raw HTTP 504 before receiving model content; the owner subsequently identified the gateway's 120-second timeout and raised it to 24 hours. Version 6 keeps the version-5 Agent behavior but explicitly routes all eleven model calls through descriptor-bound provider streaming, adds Host authorization for that mode, and connects the existing strict SSE decoder to the Broker. It pre-registers at most one whole-run replacement after a retained transport, timeout, 408, 425, 429, or 5xx failure. Memory v9 supports a sourced checkpoint candidate but does not establish association or a final Memory architecture.
changesIfSupported: Use the sourced structured checkpoint as the first simple task-resumption boundary behind the candidate Scheduler composition.
Keep richer association, consolidation, retrieval composition, and scheduling policy as independent experiments rather than embedding them in this checkpoint format.
Add deterministic duplicate, restart, malformed checkpoint, and installed-Linux composition tests before any product startup promotion.
changesIfRejected: Retain the raw run as failed or inconclusive evidence and revise the Agent action protocol, checkpoint schema, or capability budget before another frozen version.
Do not compensate by injecting task-A state into task B or the resume prompt, and do not bypass the product Module startup refusal.
prohibitedClaims: The final Memory architecture or associative recall mechanism is established.
The Agent learned or generalized from one synthetic sequence.
Linux control-group ownership or installed-package provenance passed in this canary.
Effectful tools are automatically retry-safe after an unknown provider or process outcome.
One owner Aether fixture establishes cross-model or cross-provider support.

baselines.description: The same three-phase Agent and Scheduler path receive only model-operation/v2; no storage or tool-invocation handle exists, so resume must remain explicitly unsupported.

checkpointAttemptResult.checkpointKey: echo the key from the current input

treatments.description: The Agent receives model-operation/v2 and tool-invocation/v2, stores one closed sourced checkpoint with Host approval, performs task B without tools, then lists and reads the checkpoint to resume.

frozenParameters.toolArguments: checkpoint_store, checkpoint_list, and checkpoint_get accept taskId; only the Host derives the private storage key

generatorOrDataset.contentDefinition: A fixed task-A checkpoint for release-aurora, an unrelated 29 minus 12 arithmetic task, and a resume request that contains only the task identifier and no task state.

training.name: memory-v9-historical
caseFactors: Historical Memory v9 showed that an explicit structured task checkpoint alone matched the combined candidate on its two exploratory task-resumption cases.

development.name: agent-registry-historical
caseFactors: Earlier registry canaries established the JSON-object contract, Host registry, live Aether reasoning observation, and strict response validation used unchanged here.

Task-switch version 1 retained one HTTP-200 baseline checkpoint response and then stopped because its validator confused echoing an input checkpoint key with successful persistence; no treatment or resume response was observed.

Task-switch version 2 retained eleven successful model/provider calls, one complete baseline, a stored treatment checkpoint, a correct unrelated answer, and all three closed treatment effect Runs. Resume failed because storage_list exposed an internal prefix string and the model supplied release-aurora instead of task.release-aurora. The two legal empty list results and all tool rounds remain separate failure evidence.

Task-switch version 3 retained eleven successful calls and the exact expected Agent effects, but its frozen validator rejected a semantically equal stored checkpoint because canonical storage reordered object keys. Version 3 remains inconclusive and is used only to identify this validator defect.

Task-switch version 4 again retained the exact expected effects and no actual task-A value appeared before retrieval; its frozen verifier produced a false leakage failure because the Host registry necessarily described the generic retentionHours schema field.

Task-switch version 5 retained one failed baseline request with HTTP 504 Gateway Time-out, no model content, one closed effect Run, and no case; it is infrastructure-inconclusive and cannot be merged with version 6. The owner's later gateway correction explains the 120-second boundary but does not retroactively turn that failed run into Agent evidence.

evaluation.name: aurora-sequence
caseFactors: Seed labels identify the fixed task-A and unrelated task-B inputs inside one paired sequence; the owner Aether endpoint exposes no verified provider seed control.

data.splitIsolation: No version-6 response exists before this version is frozen. Version-1 through version-5 raw artifacts remain separate inconclusive runs and cannot be merged or scored as version 6. A permitted version-6 replacement remains a separate complete run and never borrows calls or cases from its failed predecessor.

randomness.generator: Owner self-deployed Aether qwen3.6-27b fixture; temperature is omitted and the provider default is unverified.
randomness.streamSeparation: Each condition receives fresh File Core, storage namespace, tool/effect journals, process/session identifiers, and model request identifiers. Every model request uses provider streaming with no non-stream fallback. The data seed labels are not presented as provider pseudorandom seeds.
randomness.executionOrder: The single exploratory pair runs no-checkpoint first and structured-checkpoint second so a treatment failure cannot hide the baseline; order effects remain unmeasured and block comparative promotion.

primary.name: paired-task-recovery
primary.aggregation: structured-checkpoint exact recovery indicator minus no-checkpoint exact recovery indicator for the one frozen task sequence
primary.population: The single preregistered synthetic Aurora task-switch pair using the owner Aether qwen3.6-27b live fixture.

secondary.name: exact-action-sequence
secondary.aggregation: one only when treatment phases are checkpoint_store then checkpointed, answer, and checkpoint_list then checkpoint_get then resumed
secondary.population: The treatment condition's three committed Scheduler Runs.

secondary.name: actual-reasoning-observation
secondary.aggregation: one only when checkpoint and resume planning responses both contain non-empty reasoning_content decoded as observed reasoning
secondary.population: The two reasoning-required treatment planning calls.

guardrails.name: active-context-leakage
guardrails.aggregation: count of forbidden task-A checkpoint values in task-B model messages or in the first resume planning messages before storage retrieval; generic schema field names do not count
guardrails.population: The two task-B calls and first treatment resume planning call.

guardrails.name: scheduler-boundary-violations
guardrails.aggregation: count of missing commits, non-distinct Runs, Module generation changes, unsettled effects, journal failures, or recorded child processes still alive
guardrails.population: Both conditions, six Scheduler Runs, and all retained effect and tool records.

guardrails.name: capability-boundary-violations
guardrails.aggregation: count of raw storage handles, endpoint or credential values, authorization fields, capability handles, or treatment capability inventory drift
guardrails.population: Every retained artifact and all model-visible messages.

minimumEffect.intervalMethod: Descriptive one-pair exploratory canary only; no inferential interval or product promotion.
minimumEffect.comparison: Treatment must recover the exact nextAction with the checkpoint key as evidence while baseline must return resumed false and no nextAction.

execution.factorialDesign: One paired exploratory live sequence: no-checkpoint and structured-checkpoint, each containing checkpoint, unrelated, and resume Scheduler Runs in one process.

casePlan.requiredWhen: Always run the no-checkpoint condition first with all three phases.
Run structured-checkpoint only after the baseline condition completes successfully.

execution.failurePolicy: Any model, provider, SSE protocol, Scheduler, journal, storage, child-stop, source-hash, artifact, or validation failure makes the whole run failed or inconclusive; no partial stream or case becomes support.
execution.retryPolicy: Each logical model call has exactly one provider attempt and HTTP-200 content is never retried. Version 6 permits at most one fresh whole-run replacement ID only after the failed version-6 run retains a transport, timeout, HTTP 408, 425, 429, or 5xx response; all failed artifacts remain separate and no rows are merged.

stoppingRules.plannedCompletion: Stop after both conditions and all six Scheduler Runs complete, exactly eleven provider calls are retained, and the independent verifier plus all five mutations pass.
abortConditions: Abort on the first non-HTTP-200, timeout, wrong response media type, malformed or incomplete SSE response, exhausted output, Scheduler quarantine, dead letter, incomplete journal, source drift, secret leak, or recorded child that cannot be confirmed stopped.
Abort before network access unless RUN_LIVE_INTEGRATION=1 and RUN_PAID_INTEGRATION=1 are both explicitly set.
Abort before network access when the frozen preregistration, protocol, implementation, or production source digest differs.

After an eligible version-6 infrastructure failure, allow at most one separately identified whole-run replacement; after any HTTP-200 content failure or a second infrastructure failure, stop without replacement.

decisionRules.classificationOrder: First classify any infrastructure, protocol, source, privacy, evidence, or guardrail failure as inconclusive. Otherwise apply the exact treatment and baseline success predicates; no aggregate can override a guardrail.
supported: Candidate-supported only when treatment stores the exact checkpoint, task B answers 17 without context leakage, resume lists and gets the checkpoint, commits the exact nextAction and evidence key, both conditions use three distinct Runs in one process, baseline cannot resume, all effects are terminal, and five mutations are rejected.
rejected: Rejected when all evidence is structurally valid but treatment does not achieve the exact action sequence or recovery advantage over baseline.
inconclusive: Inconclusive for any endpoint, transport, timeout, provider finish, malformed output, Scheduler, process, source, journal, artifact, validation, privacy, or boundary failure, or when baseline completes but treatment is not run.

requiredChecks: Read retained artifacts, the frozen preregistration and source bytes, plus configured fixture values only for exact leakage scanning; do not import the runner or Extension.

Rebuild all eleven provider request messages, max_tokens, response_format, thinking object, model, stream=true, stream_options.include_usage=true, and omitted temperature from the corresponding model-call inputs.

Independently parse every retained SSE body, require bounded events, stable provider identity, one finish reason, terminal token usage, final [DONE], no post-terminal data, and exact equality with the Broker's accumulated final content and reasoning_content.

Verify exact baseline and treatment phase inputs, actions, results, checkpoint bytes, three distinct Runs, one Module generation, Scheduler completion, exact child stop, terminal effect records, and complete persistent tool rounds.
Reject any task-A checkpoint value in task-B messages or the first resume planning messages before retrieval while allowing generic checkpoint schema field names.

Verify every artifact and frozen source digest, token and latency accounting, secret lease release, exact capability inventories, and absence of configured URL, key, authorization, handle, baseUrl, exactUrl, or apiKey fields.

domainDesign.implementationStatus: Exploratory candidate composition with Host-validated provider streaming only; not a product Module startup path or an Extension-visible provisional progress channel.

model.endpoint: Owner Aether fixture loaded only from .env and never retained.
model.reasoningEncoding: thinking.type enabled or disabled object according to each call
model.reasoningEvidence: Only a non-empty decoded reasoning_content part proves actual reasoning.
model.providerStreaming: All eleven requests send stream=true and stream_options.include_usage=true; the Broker accepts only text/event-stream, validates chunks incrementally, requires [DONE], and returns one final accumulated result without non-stream fallback.
model.temperature: Omitted from the wire; provider default is unverified.
model.spendBasis: The owner described Aether as self-deployed with no per-call external bill; the runner still requires paid opt-in and enforces the call cap.

checkpointBoundary.extensionArguments: taskId and structured checkpoint; no storage prefix or raw key is accepted from the model
